newsitem.title: TURKEY: Honda to build second Euro plant in Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Honda to build second Euro plant in Turkey.

text.p: Turkey's leading beverage group will break the ground on Saturday to build Japanese Honda's second car plant in Europe, after Britain, to produce 30,000 units per year from late 1997.

The ceremony in Gebze, 50 km west of Istanbul, will also be attended by Turkish President Suleyman Demirel besides Nobuhiko Kawamoto, president of Honda Motor Co Ltd and officials from the local partner Anadolu Endustri Holding.
"Gebze plant of Anadolu Honda Otomotibilcilik A.S. was designed with a production capacity of 100,000 units per year," Tuncay Ozilhan, chief executive officer of the Holding, told Reuters.
Anadolu Honda is a 50-50 joint venture of Honda and Anadolu group which has been the main distributer of Honda cars in Turkey for more than 10 years.

"But we will start with a yearly capacity of 30,000 units which will require a $50 million investment," he said. "Depending on domestic and international demand, we will decide whether to build the second and third phases, with production capacities of 60,000 and 100,000, respectively."
The plant will produce Civic four-door sedans from the autumn of 1997.
Ozilhan said reaching the 100,000 capacity would require a $320 million investment, including the initial $50 million.
He said they would also move their Honda motorbike and Isuzu light truck plants to Gebze from Kartal on outskirts of Istanbul, in five years to attain bigger output capacities.
The group is also the main producer and distributer of Isuzu light trucks throught a separate joint-venture with Japan's Isuzu as well as Honda motorbikes.
"We will build a shopping center on our 157 acre land in Kartal, where our plants are currently located," Ozilhan said.
Honda's plant will the second Japanese venture in Turkey after Toyotas set up in 1990 by Sabanci Holding, Toyota Motor and Mitsui and Co and started production in late 1994.
South Korean Hyundai Motor and local Kibar Holding are also in a venture to begin producing cars in July 1997.

Turkey's leading car maker Tofas equally owned by Italy's Fiat and industrial Koc conglomerate and the second biggest producer Oyak Renault of the French Renault and the armed forces pension fund OYAK, have not worked at full capacity due to weak domestic demand which barely enlivened since the country's 1994 economic crisis.
The automotive sector was the worst hit by the crisis in 1994 when total output slumped by 41 percent to 265,837, including 212,651 cars.
Car output rose by 10 percent to 233,414 last year. Production was 137,074 units in January-August this year, versus 135,905 in the same 1995 period.
A government plan to ease car imports has recently angered producers and labour unions in the sector.

Turkish government is working on a decree to allow Turkish workers abroad who open a minimum 50,000 mark, one-year savings account in Turkey to bring in cars with a maximum age of four years without paying customs duties as part of two revenue-raising packages unveiled to fight the deficits.

The workers who open the required accounts will be able to bring cars with a maximum age of four years to Turkey without paying customs duties and also benefit from a 20 percent reduction in taxes when buying locally made cars.

"The government has taken a wrong step, but I believe it will be corrected. Such moves do not create hesitation (in ongoing investments), but shake foreign investors' trust (in government policies)," Ozilhan said, adding that no changes were made in their plant project. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-0212-2750875.
